stories.headline: Hassabis proposes US frontier-AI standards body modeled on FINRA, with pre-release model testing

key_facts.fact: Demis Hassabis laid out a proposal for a new US AI watchdog in a personal manifesto, 'A Framework for Frontier AI and the Dawning of a New Age,' published Tuesday morning (July 14).
key_facts.excerpt: Hassabis, the Nobel laureate behind Gemini, lays out the plan in a personal manifesto published Tuesday morning, 'A Framework for Frontier AI and the Dawning of a New Age.'

key_facts.fact: The body would be modeled on FINRA, the private, industry-funded watchdog that polices Wall Street under SEC oversight, funded mostly by the labs it oversees.
key_facts.excerpt: Hassabis is proposing an AI standards body modeled on FINRA (Financial Industry Regulatory Authority), the private, industry-funded watchdog that polices Wall Street under SEC oversight.

key_facts.fact: Frontier labs would initially share their models with the body voluntarily, up to 30 days before release, for safety testing of dangerous cyber, biological and 'deception' capabilities.
key_facts.excerpt: Frontier labs would initially share their models with the body voluntarily, up to 30 days before release, for safety testing that probes dangerous cyber, biological and 'deception' capabilities.

key_facts.fact: The rules would apply to all 'Frontier-class' models regardless of country of origin or whether they are open or closed, with qualifying benchmarks updated regularly.
key_facts.excerpt: The rules would apply to all frontier-class models, 'no matter their country of origin or whether they are open or closed' - with the qualifying benchmarks regularly updated as capabilities evolve.

key_facts.fact: Participation would start voluntary, but once the assessment process proves reliable, clearing the Standards Body could become a requirement for deployment in the US market.
key_facts.excerpt: In the initial phase, participation would be voluntary, with labs sharing models for review up to 30 days ahead of release. Hassabis expects that once the assessment process proves reliable, it could be formalised so that clearing the Standards Body becomes a requirement for deployment in the US market.

key_facts.excerpt: DeepSeek valued at $71B ahead of new funding round, per Financial Times

key_facts.fact: The new round would follow roughly $7 billion raised at a ~$52 billion valuation at the end of May.

stories.headline: AI video startup PixVerse closes $439M Series C extension, valuation tops $2B

key_facts.fact: Singapore-based video-generation startup PixVerse closed its Series C extension, bringing the round total to $439 million and pushing its valuation past $2 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Alibaba, others back PixVerse's extension round, Series C total at $439m

key_facts.fact: Extension-round investors include Alibaba, Lollapalooza Capital, Ivy Capital, Grand Mount Capital, Eastern Bell Capital, Mirae Asset, BlueFocus and CloudAlpha, alongside returning backers iGlobe Partners and OCBC's LionX Ventures.
key_facts.excerpt: PixVerse said that investors in the extension round include Alibaba, Lollapalooza Capital, Ivy Capital, Grand Mount Capital, Eastern Bell Capital, Mirae Asset, BlueFocus, and CloudAlpha, joining returning investors iGlobe Partners and OCBC's LionX Ventures.

key_facts.fact: PixVerse closed its initial Series C in March, led by CDH Investments, with Bloomberg reporting the amount at roughly $300 million.
key_facts.excerpt: PixVerse initially closed its Series C round in March, led by CDH Investments, with Bloomberg reporting the amount at roughly $300 million.

key_facts.fact: The company says its consumer product has over 150 million registered users and over 15 million monthly active users, and offers V-Series video, C-Series professional and R-Series world models generating video up to 4K with audio.
key_facts.excerpt: The startup said that its consumer product has over 150 million registered users and over 15 million monthly active users... a V-Series video model for consumer and API use, a C-Series video model for professional film and commercial workflows, and an R-Series of world models... generate videos in up to 4k resolution with audio baked in.

key_facts.fact: PixVerse was founded in 2023 by Wang Changhu, who previously worked at ByteDance on computer vision, and Jaden Xie.
key_facts.excerpt: The company was founded by Wang Changhu and Jaden Xie in 2023. Changhu previously worked at ByteDance on computer vision, and Xie was an executive director at investment firm Lighthouse Capital.

stories.headline: Anthropic study of 310K conversations shows Claude's values shift by model and language

key_facts.fact: Anthropic published research (Monday, July 13) measuring how Claude's expressed values vary, analyzing 309,815 anonymized Claude.ai conversations in which users gave a subjective task.
key_facts.excerpt: we sampled 309,815 Claude.ai conversations in which the user gave Claude a subjective task. Our sample drew equally from three models (Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.6, Opus 4.7) and the 20 most common languages used on Claude.ai, giving us roughly 5,000 conversations per model-language pair.

key_facts.fact: The method compressed 3,307 previously catalogued values into 339 high-level values, then reduced them via dimensionality reduction to four interpretable axes.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic's method compresses its earlier 'Values in the Wild' taxonomy - 3,307 distinct values observed in Claude's outputs - down to 339 high-level values, then reduces those to four axes using dimensionality reduction.

key_facts.fact: The four axes are Deference vs. Caution, Warmth vs. Rigor, Depth vs. Brevity, and Candor vs. Execution.
key_facts.excerpt: the company identified four key axes - Deference vs. Caution, Warmth vs. Rigor, Depth vs. Brevity, and Candor vs. Execution - that capture key behavioral patterns in Claude's responses.

key_facts.fact: Claude leans furthest toward warmth in Hindi and Arabic and furthest toward rigor in English and Russian; the axes capture roughly 15% of the variation after controlling for task, topic and the user's own values.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic reports Claude leans furthest toward warmth in Hindi and Arabic, and furthest toward rigor in English and Russian... the four axes capture roughly 15% of the variation in expressed values after controlling for task, topic and the user's own values.

key_facts.fact: The three models studied - Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.6 and Opus 4.7 - are now legacy, having been superseded by Claude Opus 4.8.
key_facts.excerpt: The three models Anthropic studied - Sonnet 4.6, Opus 4.6 and Opus 4.7 - are all now legacy... Since then, Claude Opus 4.8 [is] the [flagship].

stories.headline: Trump administration weighs framework to streamline US open-model releases as Chinese models gain

key_facts.fact: The Trump administration and industry groups are discussing a framework to streamline releases of US open models of equal or lesser capability than leading Chinese open models, per a Washington Post report.
key_facts.excerpt: the administration is discussing a structure that would streamline releases of U.S. open-source models while keeping the U.S. ahead of leading Chinese systems.

key_facts.fact: The reported framework aims to preserve US AI leadership; leading Chinese models currently trail US frontier models by an average of about seven months.
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese models currently trail U.S. frontier models by an average of seven months. Bulls argue that a ruleset built around preserving that lead could help keep capital flowing into U.S. platforms.

key_facts.fact: The discussions follow the administration's June moves restricting private frontier models: ordering Anthropic to block non-Americans from its most powerful closed models and requiring OpenAI to get government approval for each customer of GPT-5.6.
key_facts.excerpt: In early June, the Trump administration ordered Anthropic to block non-Americans from using its most powerful - and closed - models, Mythos 5 and Fable 5. Shortly after, OpenAI agreed to let the government approve every customer for its newest model, GPT-5.6.

stories.headline: Hermes agent maker Nous Research in talks to raise $75M+ at a $1.5B valuation

key_facts.fact: Nous Research, the startup behind the open-source Hermes AI agent, is in talks to raise at least $75 million in a new round, valuing it at about $1.5 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: The company is raising at least $75 million, led by Robot Ventures, with significant participation from USV and other prominent investors.

key_facts.fact: The round is led by Robot Ventures with significant participation from Union Square Ventures, and comes less than three months after Nous closed a $50 million Series A.
key_facts.excerpt: The round is led by Robot Ventures with significant participation from USV and other prominent investors... The company... closed a $50 million Series A less than three months ago.

key_facts.fact: Hermes is an open-source agent that can automate tasks like web search, coding and image understanding, and can run locally on a PC or via a cloud-hosted version.
key_facts.excerpt: Hermes is an open-source agent that can automate tasks like web search, coding, and image understanding... Hermes is open-source and can run locally on a PC or via a cloud-hosted version.

key_facts.fact: Nous Research was founded in 2023 by Jeffrey Quesnelle, Karan Malhotra, Ryan Teknium and Shivani Mitra, and had previously raised about $70 million from investors including Paradigm, North Island Ventures, OSS Capital and Balaji Srinivasan.
key_facts.excerpt: The company was founded in 2023 by Jeffrey Quesnelle, Karan Malhotra, Ryan Teknium, and Shivani Mitra. Prior to this round, it had raised a total of $70 million from investors including Paradigm, Robot Ventures, North Island Ventures, OSS Capital, and Balaji Srinivasan.
